sections.title: Prompt Cache Timer
sections.description: Claude caches your conversation to reduce costs. When idle too long the cache expires and the next message resends full context at higher cost. This shows a countdown so you know when to resume.

rows.label: Cache Timer
rows.description: Show a countdown in the sidebar after a Claude agent becomes idle.
rows.notes: Enabling also seeds cache timers for already-idle tabs.

rows.label: Timer Duration
rows.description: Match this to your provider's cache TTL. The default is 5 minutes.
rows.notes: Only shown when promptCacheTimerEnabled is on (indented under Cache Timer).

sections.title: Agent Permissions
sections.description: Choose whether Kingu launches agents with fewer permission prompts or with manual checks.
sections.notes: Header has an info tooltip: "Doesn't apply to agents where you've overridden launch arguments."

rows.label: Agent Permissions
rows.notes: Not a key of its own: the mode is derived from agentDefaultArgs/agentDefaultEnv across permission-capable agents (a 'mixed' state displays as Yolo). Choosing a mode rewrites each permission-capable agent's default args/env via applyAgentPermissionMode, skipping agents whose args were customized.

sections.notes: Empty state, shown above the lists only when detection finished, succeeded and found no agents.

rows.label: No agents detected. If one is installed, the probe may have timed out.

sections.title: Installed
sections.notes: Shown when at least one agent is detected. The header carries a '<N> detected' badge, an 'on <server name>' badge when a remote server is active, and a 'Refresh' button (tooltip 'Re-read your shell PATH and re-detect installed agents' locally, or 'Re-detect agents installed on the active server'). One row group per detected agent: icon, label, command line preview (default command struck through when overridden, plus args and env summary), and a 'Disabled' badge when disabled.

rows.label: <agent label> availability
rows.notes: Adds or removes the agent id in disabledTuiAgents (serialized update queue). Disabling the current default agent also resets defaultTuiAgent to null.

rows.label: Set default / Default
rows.notes: Only for detected and enabled agents. Shows 'Default' with a check when this agent is the default, otherwise 'Set default'.

rows.label: Docs
rows.notes: External-link icon that opens the agent's homepage URL.

rows.label: Expand command override / Collapse command override
rows.notes: Chevron that toggles the launch-defaults editor below. Starts expanded when the command, args or env differ from defaults. The editor ends with the hint 'Override the binary path or name, and edit the default launch arguments or environment for this agent.'

rows.label: Command
rows.notes: In the expanded editor. Placeholder is the default command. Commits on blur or Enter (Escape reverts). An empty value or one equal to the default deletes the override. A 'Reset' button appears when an override exists.

rows.label: Arguments
rows.notes: In the expanded editor. Placeholder is the default args or 'No default arguments'. Commits the trimmed value on blur or Enter to agentDefaultArgs[agentId]. 'Reset' restores the built-in default args.

rows.label: Environment
rows.notes: Only shown when the agent has default env vars or an env override. KEY=VALUE draft parsed into agentDefaultEnv[agentId]; placeholder is the defaults or 'No default environment'. Shows the error 'Environment text is too large to parse safely.' for oversized input. 'Reset' restores the defaults.

rows.label: Codex home to import from
rows.description: Kingu runs Codex in an isolated home. Point this at your existing Codex home to import that session history. Empty uses ~/.codex.
rows.notes: Codex row only, detected only. The description is an info tooltip ('About importing Codex history'). Scoped to the agent runtime: writes codexSessionSourceHome.host (placeholder '~/.codex') or, when the runtime default is WSL with a distro, codexSessionSourceHome.wsl[distro] (placeholder '<distro>: ~/.codex'; distro keys match case-insensitively). 'Reset' clears it. Only affects history import, not auth or config.

rows.label: <account email>
rows.description: <organization name> · <last authenticated time>

rows.label: Accounts

Copy it to finish signing in somewhere else — a private window, or another profile.' with 'Copy link' ('Copied') and 'Open' buttons.

rows.label: <account email>
rows.description: <account detail> • <last authenticated time>

Buttons: 'Install' (or 'Update' once installed; 'Preparing...' while the terminal opens) opens an inline setup terminal that runs the orchestration skill install command for the active project runtime (host or WSL) and shows the command with a 'Copy command' button and 'Press Enter to run the command.'; 'Re-check' (or 'Retry' after a failure) re-scans installed skills. When not installed: 'Prefer your own terminal? Copy install command' opens OrchestrationSkillPromptDialog, and the pre-install notice 'Before opening setup, Kingu may show a system prompt to register the Kingu CLI command on PATH.' is shown while the Kingu CLI is not on PATH. panes.title: Onboarding checklist
panes.subtitle: Finish the core workflows that make Kingu useful for parallel agent work.
panes.notes: Always rendered, including in the web client. Step completion is derived live and is not a GlobalSettings key; the per-row notes give each step's done criterion.

sections.title: Setup
sections.notes: Header shows '{done}/{total}'. Steps are numbered 1 to 6 and show a check when done. Clicking a step selects it in the detail panel.

This step has no enable toggle, so notifications.enabled and notifications.agentTaskComplete are set in the Notifications pane.

rows.description: Start new work faster with your preferred agent already selected.
rows.notes: Done when defaultTuiAgent is set and not 'blank'. The detail panel (AgentStep) shows a card grid of agents, headed 'Detected on your system · N' (agents on PATH) or 'Popular agents · N' (the first 6 catalog entries when none are detected). Remaining agents sit behind 'Show {{n}} more agents→' / 'Hide agents'. Clicking a card writes updateSettings({ defaultTuiAgent }). Warnings: 'No agents detected on your PATH…' and '<agent> isn't on your PATH yet…', with an 'Install instructions' link. A 'Yolo / Dangerously skip permissions' checkbox is rendered but is not wired in this surface: no onYoloPermissionsChange is passed, so it stays checked and does nothing.

rows.label: Enable Kingu CLI
rows.description: Register the Kingu shell command and install agent skills for browser, computer, and orchestration workflows.
rows.notes: Done when the Kingu CLI/browser skill, the computer-use skill and the orchestration skill are all installed, and Computer Use permissions are granted or unavailable. Installed skills are detected on disk via useInstalledAgentSkill. The detail panel shows three multi-select capability cards, each with an Installed/status note. A 'Full Disk Access' row appears on macOS only (badge Checking/Granted/Recommended, button 'Open Full Disk Access'). An 'Install CLI & Skills' button runs runOnboardingFeatureSetup and then shows an inline terminal with the install command. Nothing is written to GlobalSettings; it installs files and records feature interactions.

rows.label: Connect integrations
rows.description: Start an agent from a task in one click and keep PR status in view.

Step 1, 'See PR status while agents work' ('Connect a review provider so Kingu can show PR or MR status, checks, and reviews.'), holds the GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and Gitea cards. Step 2, 'Start agents on your tasks without leaving Kingu' ('Connect where your team tracks work. Kingu starts workspaces with the issue title, link, and context already attached.'), holds the Linear and Jira cards, the caption 'Your code host's issues also work as tasks.', and the GitHub and GitLab cards again. The cards are the same components as the Integrations pane, in compact setup-guide presentation. Credentials live in provider stores, not GlobalSettings.

rows.label: Automate workspace setup

Saving writes the per-repo repo.hookSettings.scripts.setup via updateRepo(), for the active git repo or the first git repo, not GlobalSettings, and sets commandSourcePolicy to 'local-only' if it is unset. A 'View in settings' link opens the repo pane's local-commands section. With no git project the hint reads 'Add a git project first, then configure the setup script for that repository.'

When connected, an account row shows the auth mode and base URL override, plus an unlink 'Disconnect Bitbucket' icon if the credential is stored. panes.notes: Always rendered (no desktop-only gate). Sections are separated by <Separator/> and each is filtered by the settings search query. 'Windows host' = isWindowsTerminalHost ?? isWindowsUserAgent() (the active terminal host, which can differ from the client OS). 'Mac' = isMacUserAgent(). Terminal appearance (theme, font, cursor) is NOT in this pane. Renderer also passes deprecated WSL props (wslAvailable/wslDistros/wslCapabilitiesLoading) which TerminalPane ignores; WSL selection lives in Project Runtime settings.

sections.title: Terminal shell
sections.description: Choose what Kingu opens for new local terminal panes.
sections.notes: Shown only when the terminal host is NOT Windows (mac/linux). Strings are hard-coded English (no translate() call). Search title 'Default shell'.

rows.label: Terminal shell
rows.notes: Mode is derived: empty/blank terminalDefaultShell = 'system'. Choosing System writes terminalDefaultShell: ''. System label shows window.api.platform.get().shell, fallback '/bin/zsh'.

rows.label: Custom shell executable
rows.description: Enter a shell name on PATH or an executable path. Kingu starts it as a login shell.
rows.notes: Visible only in Custom mode. Placeholder 'fish, nu, or /bin/zsh'. Writes on every change (trimStart). On blur, absolute paths are checked via window.api.shell.pathExists; error shows 'Shell not found: <path>. Switch to System shell or choose an executable on this host.'

sections.title: Windows Shell
sections.description: Default shell for new terminal panes on Windows.
sections.notes: Shown only when the terminal host is Windows.

rows.label: Default Shell
rows.description: Shell used when opening a new terminal pane. Takes effect for new terminals.
rows.notes: Each option has a shell icon. Default 'powershell.exe'. Git Bash shown when Git for Windows bash.exe is detected OR is the current value; disabled when not detected. WSL shown only when it is already the current value, and is always disabled (distro selection moved to Project Runtime).

sections.title: Rendering
sections.description: Terminal renderer behavior for live panes and new panes.

rows.label: GPU Acceleration
rows.description: Auto tries WebGL, with DOM fallback for unsupported or risky renderers.
rows.notes: Default 'auto'. Description changes with value: on = 'WebGL is always attempted for terminal panes.'; off = 'WebGL disabled; DOM renderer for max compatibility.'

rows.label: Color Contrast
rows.description: Balances readability with your terminal theme. Recommended.
rows.notes: Mode derived from value: undefined = Automatic, 1 = Off, anything else = Custom. Automatic writes undefined, Off writes 1, Custom writes last custom value (initially 4.5). Description per mode: Off = 'Keeps program colors unchanged, including dim text and Powerline separators.'; Custom = 'Choose how much to increase contrast between text and its background.'

rows.label: Contrast target
rows.description: Higher values increase contrast where possible. Background colors stay unchanged.
rows.notes: Visible only when Color Contrast = Custom. A number field (min 1, max 21, step 0.1, suffix ':1') plus a slider (min 1.1, max 21, step 0.1; commits on release) with end labels 'Subtle' / 'Strong'.

sections.title: Terminal Interaction
sections.description: Mouse and clipboard behavior for terminal panes.

rows.label: Scroll Speed
rows.description: Adjust how wheel input feels in scrollback and in mouse-aware terminal apps.
rows.notes: Group header with a 'Reset' button that restores all three sliders to defaults: Normal 1.15, Fast 5, TUI 1. The three sliders below sit in a 3-column grid.

rows.label: Normal
rows.description: Scrollback wheel multiplier.
rows.notes: min 0.5, max 3, step 0.05, value shown with suffix 'x'. Default 1.15.

rows.label: Fast
rows.description: Extra multiplier while scrolling with a modifier key.
rows.notes: min 1, max 10, step 0.5, suffix 'x'. Default 5.

rows.label: TUI
rows.description: Discrete wheel reports for full-screen terminal apps.
rows.notes: min 1, max 10, step 1, suffix 'x'. Default 1.

rows.label: Right-click to paste
rows.description: Right-click pastes the clipboard. Ctrl+right-click opens the context menu.
rows.notes: On macOS the description reads 'Right-click pastes the clipboard. Control-click opens the context menu.' Shown on all platforms (its search entry lives in terminal-windows-search).

rows.label: Focus Follows Mouse
rows.description: Hovering a terminal pane activates it without needing to click.

rows.label: Copy on Select
rows.description: Automatically copy terminal selections to the clipboard.

rows.label: Trim Gutter on Copy
rows.description: Drop the left gutter agent output is painted behind, so copied text is not indented. Only the indent every selected line shares is removed.

rows.label: Allow TUI Clipboard Writes (OSC 52)
rows.description: Let programs in the terminal (Zellij, tmux, Neovim, fzf, Grok, SSH) copy to your system clipboard.
rows.notes: Carries a deep-link anchor id (OSC52_CLIPBOARD_SETTING_ID) used by terminal prompts that link here.

sections.title: Workspace Setup Script
sections.description: Where the repository setup script runs when a new workspace is created.

rows.label: Setup Script Location
rows.description: "New Tab" opens the setup command in a background tab titled "Setup" without stealing focus.
rows.notes: Toggle group; deselecting is ignored.

sections.title: Manage Sessions
sections.description: Recover from a frozen or misbehaving terminal by killing sessions or restarting the underlying daemon.
sections.notes: Header is a plain h3/p, not SettingsSubsectionHeader. Deep-link anchor id 'terminal-manage-sessions'. Data comes from window.api.pty.management (listSessions, killOne, macTccAttribution) and the daemon actions hook; nothing here is a GlobalSettings key.

rows.label: macOS permission grants aren’t reaching terminals
rows.description: The terminal daemon was started by an Kingu install that no longer exists, so macOS can’t attribute its commands to Kingu — Accessibility and Automation grants are silently ignored (osascript fails with error -25211). Restarting the daemon fixes this; running terminal sessions will close.
rows.notes: Amber alert, shown only when macTccAttribution() reports health 'severed' (effectively macOS after an app update replaced the binary). Re-checked on window focus and after a daemon restart. The 'Open Manage Sessions' button is hidden here (shown only where the notice appears elsewhere).

rows.label: Sessions (<count>)
rows.notes: Table of live PTY sessions: status dot (alive = green), workspace name, session id, and a per-row X 'Kill session <id>' button that opens a kill confirmation dialog (ManageSessionKillDialog). Clicking a row with a known tab navigates to that terminal ('Go to terminal <workspace>') and closes Settings. Empty states: 'Loading…', 'No sessions.' Max height 360px, scrolls. Toasts: 'Killed session.', 'Couldn’t kill session — it may already be gone.', 'Couldn’t load sessions.'

rows.label: Refresh
rows.notes: Icon button next to the Sessions count; re-lists sessions. Disabled while busy or refreshing.

rows.label: Kill all sessions
rows.notes: Icon button with tooltip; opens the daemon 'killAll' confirmation dialog (DaemonActionDialog). Disabled when busy or no sessions. Optimistically clears the list.

rows.label: Restart daemon
rows.notes: Icon button with tooltip; opens the daemon 'restart' confirmation dialog. Also the remedy for the macOS attribution notice.

sections.title: Advanced
sections.description: Scrollback, word boundaries, and platform-specific terminal behaviors.

rows.label: Scrollback Rows
rows.description: Retained desktop terminal rows for new and open panes.
rows.notes: Presets from SCROLLBACK_PRESETS_ROWS (DESKTOP_TERMINAL_SCROLLBACK_ROW_PRESETS). Preset vs Custom is transient UI state (scrollbackMode in use-settings-store-model, default 'preset', not persisted); a non-preset stored value also shows Custom. Choosing Custom reveals a number input: min 1000, max 50000, step 100, suffix 'rows', committed on blur/Enter and clamped by normalizeDesktopTerminalScrollbackRows.

rows.label: Word Separators
rows.description: Characters treated as word boundaries for double-click selection.
rows.notes: Monospace input, placeholder " ()[]{},'"`". Empty string writes undefined (falls back to default).

rows.label: PowerShell Version
rows.description: Choose between Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7+ for new terminal panes.
rows.notes: Shown only when the terminal host is Windows AND terminalWindowsShell is 'powershell.exe'. Default 'auto'. 'PowerShell 7+' is disabled when pwsh.exe is not installed; then the description reads 'Auto uses Windows PowerShell now and switches to PowerShell 7+ when installed.' plus a 'Download PowerShell 7+' link to github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases/latest.

rows.label: Option as Alt
rows.description: Auto — detected: <layout>.
rows.notes: macOS only. Auto description embeds the detected layout: 'US English — Option sends Alt/Esc sequences', 'non-US layout — Option composes characters like @, €, [, ]', or 'unknown layout — Option composes characters (safe default)'. Off = 'Option composes special characters for your keyboard layout.'; Both = 'Both Option keys send Alt/Esc sequences.'; Left/Right = 'The <left|right> Option key sends Alt/Esc; the other composes special characters.'

rows.label: JIS Yen (¥) to Backslash (\\)
rows.description: Pressing the JIS Yen (¥) key sends a backslash (\\) instead.
rows.notes: macOS only. Default false. The fallback string in source contains a doubled backslash (TS literal '\\\\'); it is meant to render a single backslash character.

panes.title: Quick Commands
panes.subtitle: Saved terminal commands, scoped globally or per project.
panes.notes: Always rendered. A list manager, not a form: the pane has no subsection headers. Commands for the local host are stored in GlobalSettings.terminalQuickCommands (written via store upsertTerminalQuickCommand/deleteTerminalQuickCommand, not updateSettings directly); commands for a remote Kingu server (runtime environment) are stored on that server and loaded per connection. Renderer also passes quickCommandAddIntentSignal, a one-shot deep-link that opens the Add dialog on mount.

sections.notes: Toolbar + command list.

rows.label: Commands are saved on the selected Kingu host, then scoped globally or to a project setup. Commands from this device also remain available in remote workspaces.
rows.notes: Ownership explainer text, shown only when more than one host is configured (local + remote servers).

rows.label: Search commands
rows.notes: Local filter over the list (search icon, placeholder 'Search commands'); not persisted.

rows.label: All commands
rows.notes: Scope filter: multi-select combobox popover. Trigger label is 'All commands' when all are selected, otherwise e.g. 'Global, <project> +N' ('None' fallback). The empty selection is forbidden; clicking 'All commands' while all are selected collapses to Global only. Local UI state, not persisted.

rows.label: Saved on
rows.notes: Host picker, shown only when more than one host is configured. Options come from getTerminalQuickCommandHostOptions (configured hosts + runtime environments; labels can be overridden). Changing it resets the scope filter. Not a setting.

rows.label: Add Command
rows.notes: Opens the Add Quick Command dialog. The draft scope follows the filter: a single selected project becomes that project, Global-only becomes Global, otherwise the active project, falling back to Global. Disabled for a remote host whose commands are not loaded or not supported.

rows.label: Update this Kingu server to manage its quick commands.
rows.notes: Remote host only: shown in place of the list when the server does not support quick commands. Other remote states: 'Could not load commands from this host.' with a 'Retry' button; 'Loading commands…'; and, above a stale list, 'Could not refresh commands from this host. Showing the last loaded commands.' with 'Retry'.

rows.label: <command label>
rows.description: <command text, or '<Agent>: <prompt>' for agent commands>
rows.notes: One row per command: label ('Untitled' if empty), scope badge ('Global', a project name with its color, or 'Missing project'), body ('No command text' if empty), and a run-mode label ('Enter', 'Insert' or 'Agent'). Hover actions: Edit (opens the dialog), Copy (copies the body; 'Copied' or 'Couldn't copy'), Remove (confirmation 'Delete "<label>"?' / 'This quick command will be removed from your saved list.' / 'Delete'). Empty states: 'No quick commands saved.' + 'Run them from the Quick Commands button in the tab bar, or right-click inside any terminal.'; 'No commands in the selected scopes.'; 'No commands match this search.'

sections.title: Add Quick Command
sections.description: Saved items appear in the tab bar menu for one-click run.
sections.notes: Modal dialog (TerminalQuickCommandDialog) opened by Add Command or Edit; the title is 'Edit Quick Command' when editing. Fields edit a draft TerminalQuickCommand, which Save writes to the selected host's list (local = terminalQuickCommands). In Settings the Advanced section starts expanded. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter saves.

rows.label: Label
rows.notes: Placeholder 'Start dev server'. Required for Save. Field: label.

rows.label: Action
rows.notes: Aria labels 'Terminal Command' / 'Agent Prompt'. Field: action. Switching keeps separate drafts for each action.

rows.label: Agent
rows.notes: Only when Action = Agent. Placeholder 'Choose agent'. Agents that cannot take prompt commands are listed but disabled with 'Does not support prompt commands'. Field: agent.

rows.label: Command
rows.notes: Large resizable editor (14 rows) with the footer hint 'Drag corner to resize'. For Terminal: header 'Command', monospace, placeholder 'npm run dev', field command. For Agent: header 'Prompt', header hint 'Supports /goal, skills, paths', placeholder 'Ask the agent to investigate this workspace', footer hint 'Multi-line prompts are fine — keep them focused.', field prompt. Required for Save.

rows.label: Append Enter — run immediately
rows.notes: Only when Action = Terminal; compact switch in the editor footer. Default on. Field: appendEnter (off = 'Insert' only).

rows.label: Scope
rows.notes: Inside the collapsible 'Advanced' toggle (when collapsed it shows '· <scope summary>'). Project is disabled when the host has no projects. When Project is chosen, a project select appears (placeholder 'Choose project', or 'Project not in list' plus the note 'Saving keeps the existing project scope unless you choose another.' if the stored project is missing). Field: scope.

rows.label: Save
rows.notes: Footer buttons 'Cancel' and 'Save' (Save shows its shortcut label; tooltip 'Save (<shortcut>)'). Save is disabled until Label and Command/Prompt are filled in (and, for Agent, a supported agent is chosen).

panes.title: Browser
panes.subtitle: Home page, link routing, and session cookies.
panes.notes: Pane only rendered when model.showDesktopOnlySettings (= !isWebClient), i.e. hidden in the web client. Every row is individually filtered by the settings search query (matchesSettingsSearch against browser-search / browser-use-search entries). Home page, search engine, zoom and Kagi link are NOT GlobalSettings: they are persisted UI-state keys (browserDefaultUrl, browserDefaultSearchEngine, browserDefaultZoomLevel, browserKagiSessionLink) written via store setters -> window.api.ui.set(...).

sections.title: Agent Browser Use
sections.description: Let coding agents drive this browser with your logins.
sections.notes: Collapsed state (feature off) shows only the title, description and the enable switch. When enabled it becomes a card whose description reads 'Let coding agents drive this browser with your logins. Finish the three steps below.' plus a progress chip '{completed}/3' (CLI enabled, skill detected, default-profile cookies imported). Enable state is stored in localStorage key 'kingu.browserUse.enabled' ('1'/'0'), not GlobalSettings.

rows.label: Enable Agent Browser Use
rows.notes: Switch aria-label. Persisted to localStorage 'kingu.browserUse.enabled'; turning on records feature interaction 'agent-browser-setup' and triggers CLI status + browser profile fetch.

rows.label: Use an existing browser session
rows.description: If cookie import is not the right fit, Computer Use can control local apps and may use existing logged-in browser sessions where applicable. Install the Computer Use skill; macOS also requires privacy permissions.
rows.notes: Button 'Open Computer Use' navigates to Computer Use settings (actions.openComputerUseFromBrowser). Only when enabled and onOpenComputerUse is provided.

rows.label: Enable Kingu CLI
rows.description: Registers the Kingu CLI command so agents can orchestrate the browser from their shell.
rows.notes: Step 1 (step badge). Action button label: 'Enable' / 'Registering...' / 'Enabled' (disabled once done) / 'Fix PATH' (installed but PATH not configured). Shows 'Installed at <path>' when enabled; amber detail when PATH needs attention; tooltip with detail when unsupported. Uses window.api.cli install status (WSL variant when active project runtime is WSL). Search title: 'Register the Kingu CLI so agents can drive the browser.'

rows.label: Browser Use skill
rows.description: Enables agents to navigate and verify pages in Kingu's browser.
rows.notes: Step 2, wrapped in SearchableSetting 'Install Browser Use Skill' / "Install the Browser Use skill so agents can operate Kingu's browser." AgentSkillSetupPanel inline: status 'Installed'/'Not installed'/'Checking...'/'Setup failed', copyable install command, 'Install'/'Update' button opening an embedded setup terminal, 'Re-check'/'Retry'. Dimmed/disabled when step blocked (install disabled reason, or neither CLI nor skill present).

rows.label: Import Browser Cookies
rows.description: Bring your existing logins into Kingu so agents can reach authenticated pages. Imports into the default profile.
rows.notes: Step 3. Dropdown button 'Import' / 'Re-import' with items 'From {browser}' (submenu of browser profiles when >1) and 'From File…', plus machine notice and disclosure. Shows 'Last imported from {source}' and link 'Manage profiles for separate logins' (scrolls to Session & Cookies). Dimmed when blocked. Search description: 'Import cookies from Chrome, Edge, or other browsers so agents can reuse your logins.'

rows.label: Try it — example prompts
rows.description: Paste any of these into Claude Code, Codex, or another agent in a project where the skill is installed.
rows.notes: Three static example prompts, each with a 'Copy' icon button (copies to clipboard). Only when Agent Browser Use enabled.

sections.notes: General browser rows, headerless, rendered in this order directly after Agent Browser Use.

rows.label: Default Home Page
rows.description: URL opened when creating a new browser tab. Leave empty to open a blank tab.
rows.notes: Not GlobalSettings: UI-state key browserDefaultUrl (setBrowserDefaultUrl -> window.api.ui.set). Text input (placeholder 'https://google.com') + 'Save' button; empty saves null (blank tab); value normalized; toast 'Home page saved.'

rows.label: Default Search Engine
rows.description: Used when typing non-URL text in the address bar.
rows.notes: Not GlobalSettings: UI-state key browserDefaultSearchEngine (google stored as null). Search description: 'Search engine used when typing non-URL text in the address bar.'

rows.label: Kagi private session link
rows.description: Optional private session link for Kagi auth.
rows.notes: Only shown under the search-engine select when 'kagi' is selected. Password input (placeholder 'https://kagi.com/search?token=...') + 'Save' + 'Clear' (Clear only when a link is stored). Not GlobalSettings: UI-state key browserKagiSessionLink.

rows.label: Default Zoom
rows.description: Applied to newly opened browser tabs.
rows.notes: Not GlobalSettings: UI-state key browserDefaultZoomLevel (Electron zoom level, default 0). Labels = round(100*1.2^level)%. Search description: 'Zoom level applied to newly opened browser tabs.'

rows.label: Browser identity
rows.description: Choose the user agent for every browser profile and page. Native mode disables Google sign-in. Changes take effect after a restart.
rows.notes: Not GlobalSettings: read/written via window.api.browser.identityGet()/identitySet(mode). Tooltips: Cleaned = 'Removes Kingu and Electron tokens to match imported Chrome sessions.'; Native = "Keeps Electron's built-in identity for sites that reject the cleaned identity. Google sign-in is unavailable in Native mode." Shows 'Restart required' after change. If settings-focused host is not local: shows text 'Manage browser identity on the remote host with the Kingu CLI.' instead. While loading: 'Loading…'. If configuredMode is null: error text 'Identity data must be reset explicitly before it can be changed.' + 'Reset it from the command line: kingu browser identity set --mode <mode> --reset'.

rows.label: Link Routing
rows.description: Open http(s) links in Kingu's built-in browser — from the terminal, markdown, and the editor. {{shortcut}} always uses your system browser.
rows.notes: shortcut = '⇧⌘-click' on Mac, 'Shift+Ctrl+click' elsewhere. When openLinksInAppModifierInverts is true, description drops the last sentence. Toggle also writes openLinksInAppPreferencePrompted: true.

rows.label: Hold Shift to open in Kingu
rows.description: Links open in your system browser. When enabled, {{chord}}+click opens one in Kingu's built-in browser instead.
rows.notes: Indented under Link Routing. Label/description depend on openLinksInApp: when openLinksInApp is true label is 'Hold Shift to open in your web browser' and description 'Links open in Kingu, so {{chord}}+click sends one to your system browser instead.' chord = '⇧⌘' (Mac) or 'Shift+Ctrl'.

rows.label: Show link actions
rows.description: Show available actions when you click a link in the terminal or a chat transcript. Turn this off to require {{modifier}}-click in the terminal.
rows.notes: Indented row. modifier = '⌘' on Mac, 'Ctrl' elsewhere. Absent/undefined treated as on (checked unless === false).

rows.label: Localhost Worktree Labels
rows.description: Open workspace ports as worktree-specific Kingu localhost URLs so browser tabs are easier to tell apart.
rows.notes: Checked only when === true (default off).

sections.title: Remote browsing
sections.description: Where remote workspace pages render, and where their network traffic leaves from.
sections.notes: Header shown when either child row matches the search query.

rows.label: Remote server workspaces
rows.description: Where pages render. Traffic always goes through the remote server. Applies to new pages only.
rows.notes: device => browserClientHostedRemoteEnabled: true; server => false. Absent treated as 'device'. Tooltips: 'Pages render on this desktop, so input and popups behave natively.' / 'Pages render on the remote server and stream to this device.'

rows.label: SSH workspaces
rows.description: Where browser traffic leaves from. Pages always render on this device.
rows.notes: host => browserSshWorkspaceRoutingEnabled: true; device => false; absent treated as 'host'. Tooltips: "Traffic and DNS go through the workspace's SSH host." / "Pages browse from this machine's network." When browserSshWorkspaceRoutingDisabledTargetIds is non-empty, a sub-list 'Hosts browsing from this device instead:' shows each SSH target label with a 'Use SSH host' link that removes it from that array.

sections.title: Session & Cookies
sections.description: Select a default profile for new browser tabs. Import cookies and switch profiles per-tab via the ··· toolbar menu.
sections.notes: Anchor id 'browser-session-cookies'. Search description: 'Manage browser profiles and import cookies from Chrome, Edge, Comet, or other browsers.' None of these rows are GlobalSettings: profiles live in the browser store slice (browserSessionProfiles via main-process IPC); the default profile id is store state defaultBrowserSessionProfileId(ByHostId).

rows.label: Add Profile
rows.notes: Opens 'New Browser Profile' dialog: 'Profile name' input (max 50), 'Cancel' / 'Create' ('Creating…'); creates an isolated session profile via createBrowserSessionProfile('isolated', name).

rows.label: Host
rows.description: This computer
rows.notes: Only shown when more than one host option exists (local + runtime/Kingu server hosts; SSH hosts excluded). Options are dynamic host labels; description is selected host detail ('This computer' for local, 'Browser profiles on this Kingu server.' for runtime; fallback 'Browser profiles for the selected host.'). Writes store browserSessionHostIdOverride via setBrowserSessionHostId.

rows.label: Default
rows.description: No cookies imported
rows.notes: Profile list: always a 'Default' profile row, then each non-default profile. Clicking a row makes it the active default for new tabs (badge 'Active'); subtitle is the cookie source '{Browser} ({profile})' or 'No cookies imported'. Each row has an 'Import Cookies' dropdown ('From {browser}' submenus, 'From File…'). Default row has a trash button that clears default cookies (disabled if none imported, toast 'Default cookies cleared.'); other rows have a trash button that deletes the profile (toast 'Profile "{name}" removed.').

panes.title: Mobile Emulator
panes.subtitle: Configure mobile emulator support for Kingu and coding agents.
panes.notes: Pane only rendered when model.showDesktopOnlySettings (= !isWebClient). Availability comes from runtime RPC 'emulator.availability' on the local host, refreshed on mount.

sections.notes: Headerless group (SearchableSetting titled 'Mobile Emulator' for search only).

rows.label: Enable Mobile Emulator
rows.description: Shows the New Mobile Emulator action and allows agents to attach to the active emulator.
rows.notes: Absent treated as enabled (checked unless === false).

rows.label: Availability
rows.description: Checking Android SDK and iOS Simulator support.
rows.notes: Status badge: 'Disabled' (feature off) / 'Checking...' / 'Ready' / 'Needs setup'; icon button 'Refresh emulator availability'. Description is dynamic: '1 emulator device detected.' / '{n} emulator devices detected.' when available, else the simctl/serve-sim/general error message.

rows.label: Android SDK
rows.description: Not found. Install Android Studio, then create a Virtual Device.
rows.notes: Toolchain status sub-row under Availability; only when enabled and availability loaded. When found: 'Using configured path <path>' or 'Detected at <path>'. Actions: 'Download Android Studio' (only when not found; opens https://developer.android.com/studio), 'Locate SDK folder' (directory picker -> androidSdkPath, then re-checks), 'Clear' (only when a path is configured; sets androidSdkPath null).

rows.label: iOS Simulator (Xcode)
rows.description: Install Xcode and add an iOS Simulator runtime.
rows.notes: Only on macOS (availability.platform === 'darwin') and when enabled. Shows 'Ready' when simctl and serve-sim are OK, else their message or the fallback description.

rows.label: Default Device
rows.description: Default device for new emulator tabs and agent attach commands. Auto-select prefers an already running device.
rows.notes: Plus one dynamic option per detected device (value = UDID, label = device name with state suffix e.g. '(Booted)', Android/iOS icon; unavailable devices disabled). Auto-select stores null. Disabled when emulator is off. Description when no devices: 'Kingu will auto-select an emulator device after devices are detected.'

sections.title: Agent Mobile Emulator Control
sections.description: Let coding agents control the active mobile emulator with Kingu CLI commands.
sections.notes: Only shown when mobileEmulatorEnabled is not false. Card with progress chip '{completed}/2' (CLI enabled + Kingu CLI skill installed).

rows.label: Enable Kingu CLI
rows.description: Registers the Kingu CLI command so agents can control the active emulator from their shell.
rows.notes: Step 1. Button label 'Enable' / 'Registering...' / 'Enabled' / 'Fix PATH'. Shows 'Installed at <path>' when enabled; while busy 'Registering the Kingu CLI <path> so emulator commands can run from agent shells.'

rows.label: Kingu CLI skill
rows.description: Enables agents to use Kingu CLI commands, including mobile emulator control.
rows.notes: Step 2. AgentSkillSetupPanel inline (status, copy command, Install/Update in embedded terminal, Re-check). Opening hint 'Checking Kingu CLI before opening skill setup.' Dimmed when blocked. Commands built for the local host only.

rows.label: Common emulator commands
rows.description: Commands target the active emulator for the current worktree. Coordinates are normalized from 0..1.
rows.notes: Static code snippets: 'kingu emulator list --json', 'kingu emulator attach "iPhone 16 Pro" --json', 'kingu emulator tap 0.5 0.7 --json', 'kingu emulator type "hello" --json'.

rows.label: Try it — example prompts
rows.description: Paste any of these into Claude Code, Codex, or another agent in a project where the Kingu CLI skill is installed.
rows.notes: Three static example prompts with 'Copy' icon buttons.

panes.title: Floating Workspace
panes.subtitle: Global terminal, browser, and markdown tabs.
panes.notes: Rendered on all clients (no desktop-only gate). Whole pane returns null if the search query matches none of its entries; in the web client the 'browser' keyword is excluded from search.

sections.notes: Headerless group (SearchableSetting 'Floating Workspace' / 'Enable the floating workspace and choose where new tabs start.' for search only).

rows.label: Enable Floating Workspace
rows.description: Shows the floating workspace button and panel.
rows.notes: Records feature interaction 'floating-workspace' (on) or 'floating-workspace-hidden' (off).

rows.label: Terminal Directory
rows.description: New floating terminal tabs start here. Markdown notes are saved in Kingu's app-owned floating workspace.
rows.notes: Read-only input (placeholder '~') showing '~' when unset/'~', otherwise the resolved path from window.api.app.getFloatingTerminalCwd. Folder icon button 'Choose floating workspace directory' opens window.api.app.pickFloatingWorkspaceDirectory() and writes floatingTerminalCwd; no free-text entry.

rows.label: Toggle Button Location
rows.description: The keyboard shortcut works regardless of where the toggle is shown.
rows.notes: ToggleGroup single-select; defaults to 'floating-button' when unset; empty deselect ignored.

panes.title: Appearance
panes.subtitle: Theme, zoom, app and terminal appearance, sidebars, and status bar.
panes.notes: Pane is three independently collapsible accordion cards (all expanded by default; each header shows an icon, title and a one-line summary) followed by a headerless App Icon row. An active settings search force-opens matching cards and every 'Advanced' disclosure, and hides non-matching rows. Advanced disclosures (label 'Advanced') are collapsed by default. TerminalContrastSetting is NOT rendered here (it lives in the Terminal pane's rendering section). There is intentionally no Code & Markdown card.

sections.title: Interface
sections.notes: Accordion card (AppWindow icon). Header summary is dynamic: '<Theme> · <Language> · <IDE font or 'Default font'>'.

rows.label: Theme
rows.notes: Also calls applyTheme() immediately. Search description: 'Choose how Kingu looks in the app window.'

rows.label: Language
rows.notes: Shown because SHOW_UI_LANGUAGE_SETTING = true. Values are the UI_LANGUAGE_* constants from shared/ui-language.ts. Installed plugin language packs are appended as extra items labelled '<locale> — <pluginKey>' with value = pack id. Search description: 'Choose the language used by the Kingu interface.'

panes.subtitle: repo.path of the switcher-selected host's repo (the project's filesystem path on that host)
panes.notes: One pane per project in the sidebar 'Projects' group (model.settingsProjectList); id is repo-<settingsProject.representativeRepoId>. Title is translate('auto.components.settings.Settings.3bf149e873', 'Project Settings > {{value0}}') with value0 = project.displayName. The pane renders the repo row for the host currently chosen in 'Available Hosts' (settingsProjectHostSelection / settingsProjectSetupSelection), and every edit is bound to that host (updateRepo(repo.id, updates, { hostId })). Most rows write Repo fields via updateRepo; Project Runtime writes a Project field via updateProject; sparse presets live in persisted app state; the issue command is a file in the repo. Sections are separated by <Separator/> and each section is hidden when the settings search does not match its entries (unless the query matches the project name/path, which forces the whole pane visible). FOLDER projects (repo.kind folder) show only the Identity section's Remove Project, Display Name and Project Icon rows; every other section and row requires a git repo.

sections.title: Identity
sections.description: Project-specific display details for the sidebar and tabs.
sections.notes: The header also shows 'Type:' followed by getRepoKindLabel(repo) ('Git' or 'Folder'). For folder repos an extra line reads 'Opened as folder. Git features are unavailable for this workspace.' Available Hosts, Project Runtime, Keep Fork Up to Date, External worktrees, Default Worktree Base and Worktree Location are rendered inside this section only for git (non-folder) repos.

rows.label: Remove Project
rows.description: Remove this project from Kingu on all configured hosts.
rows.notes: Action, not a setting: a trash icon button in the top-right of the Identity header. The first click arms it (it turns destructive and the tooltip/aria-label become 'Confirm Remove Project'); a second click calls model.removeProjectAllHosts(settingsProject.setups). Blurring the button cancels the confirmation.

rows.label: Display Name
rows.description: Project-specific display details for the sidebar and tabs.
rows.notes: RepoSettingsDraftInput saves on every keystroke, but holds the save during IME composition and flushes on blur or unmount.

rows.label: Repo Icon
rows.description: Project icon and color used in the sidebar and tabs.
rows.notes: The searchable title is 'Project Icon'. The row shows a preview glyph and the current icon label: 'GitHub avatar', the custom image label or 'Custom image', '<emoji> emoji', '<Icon> icon with repo color', or 'Default'. The 'Reset' button re-resolves the GitHub avatar and writes it (with upstream), or clears repoIcon to null when no GitHub remote exists. On mount the pane refreshes the upstream/avatar metadata when a GitHub avatar is set or when repo.upstream is undefined.

rows.label: Color
rows.notes: Eight preset swatches (REPO_COLORS; the swatches show no text, and the aria-label reads 'Use {{value0}} repo color'), plus a ColorPicker whose trigger reads 'Custom'. Its aria-label is 'Choose custom repo color', or 'Custom repo color {{value0}}' when the current color is not a preset, and the hex shows in the trigger in that case. The default is #737373.

rows.label: Icon source tabs (Avatar / Icon / Emoji)
rows.notes: UI-only tab switcher; the choice is not persisted. The initial tab is 'emoji' for an emoji icon, 'icon' for a lucide icon, and 'avatar' otherwise.

rows.label: Use GitHub Avatar
rows.description: Used by default — GitHub always provides one, even when the owner hasn't set a custom image.
rows.notes: Avatar tab. Resolves the GitHub remote live on the repo's owning host. Toasts 'No GitHub remote found for this repo.' or 'Failed to resolve the GitHub repo.' on failure.

rows.label: Upload PNG
rows.description: PNG uploads must be 256KB or smaller.
rows.notes: Avatar tab. Opens the native picker (window.api.shell.pickRepoIconImage) and sets repoIcon = {type:'image', source:'upload', src:dataUrl, label:fileName}. Toasts 'Failed to import repo icon' on error.

rows.label: Favicon
rows.description: PNG uploads must be 256KB or smaller.
rows.notes: Avatar tab. A website text input (placeholder 'example.com') plus a 'Favicon' button, which sets repoIcon = {type:'image', source:'favicon', label:'Website favicon'}. Toasts 'Enter a valid website URL.' for an invalid URL. The input itself is local state and is not persisted.

rows.label: Icon
rows.notes: Icon tab: a 10-column grid of Lucide icon buttons (getRepoLucideIconOptions), each with a tooltip of the icon label and the aria-label 'Use {{value0}} repo icon'. Sets repoIcon = {type:'lucide', name}.

rows.label: Emoji
rows.notes: Emoji tab: a lazy-loaded emoji-picker-react picker (search placeholder 'Search emoji') that follows Kingu's theme. Sets repoIcon = {type:'emoji', emoji}. Toasts "This emoji can't be used as a repo icon." when the emoji exceeds 16 chars. When one is selected it shows 'Current: {{value0}}'.

rows.label: Available Hosts
rows.description: Project paths and worktree settings are host-specific; creating a workspace can target any ready setup.
rows.notes: Git repos only. Hidden unless the project has more than one host setup or at least one configured host where it is not yet set up. The search description is 'Hosts where this project is set up.' Each setup row shows the host label ('{{value0}} via {{value1}}' for SSH nested under a runtime), a state badge and the path (or 'Path pending'). Badge values: Ready, Not set up, Setting up, Error, Unsupported, Disconnected, 'Workspace window closed', Unknown. When the owner window is closed, the row also says 'The server is reachable but its Kingu window is closed. Open Kingu on {{value0}} to use this setup.' The current setup shows a 'Current' badge. Other openable setups show an 'Open' button that switches the viewed host. Setups with no repo (placeholders) show a 'Remove' button (deleteProjectHostSetup). Project host setups are app/project state, not Repo fields.

rows.label: Viewing host
rows.notes: Shown in the Available Hosts header only when more than one openable setup exists. It sets the ephemeral per-project selection (setSettingsProjectHostSelection), which re-renders the whole pane for that host's repo. Not persisted to the repo.

rows.label: Host availability
rows.description: Add this same project on another connected host.
rows.notes: Action. Shown when at least one configured host lacks this project. The 'Add to another host' button opens the inline 'Add project to host' panel (description 'Choose where this project should also be available.', with a 'Close' X). The panel holds: a 'Host' select listing configured hosts without a setup (unavailable hosts are disabled and show a detail such as 'Kingu server version is incompatible', 'Checking host capabilities', 'Update Kingu on this host to set up projects' or 'Connect this host before importing or cloning the project'); then three choices, 'Browse folder' ('Use an existing checkout or folder on this host.') and, under 'Other ways to add', 'Clone from URL' ('Clone this repository onto the selected host.') and 'Add host placeholder' ('Remember this host and finish adding the project later.'). The 'Existing folder' step has a path input (placeholder '/path/to/project/on/host'), a kind select with git = 'Git repo' and folder = 'Folder', and an 'Add project' button ('Adding...' while busy); it calls setupProjectExistingFolder. The 'Clone from URL' step has 'Repository URL' and '/destination/on/host' inputs and a 'Clone' button ('Cloning...'); it calls setupProjectClone. The 'Add host placeholder' step explains 'This only records that the project should be available on this host. You can add the folder or clone later.' and has an 'Add {{host}}' button; it calls createProjectHostSetup with setupState not-set-up.

rows.label: Project runtime
rows.description: Dynamic: 'No project override. General settings select Windows.' | 'This project runs on Windows.' | 'No project override. General settings select {{value0}} via WSL.' | 'This project runs in {{value0}} via WSL.' | repair text ('WSL is not available. Switch this project to Windows or repair WSL.' / '{{value0}} is not installed in WSL. Choose an installed distro or switch this project to Windows.' / 'Choose a WSL distro or switch this project to Windows.')
rows.notes: Searchable title 'Project Runtime', description 'Choose whether this project runs on Windows or WSL.' Git repos only, on the local execution host on a Windows terminal host (isLocalWindowsProject). Writes the Project field through updateProject, not a Repo field: inherit-global = undefined, windows-host = {kind:'windows-host'}, wsl = {kind:'wsl', distro}. Reads GlobalSettings localWindowsRuntimeDefault for the 'Default (...)' label. WSL is disabled while capabilities load, when WSL is unavailable, or when no distro exists. Help text: 'Runtime changes apply to new terminals, agent checks, and skill discovery for this project. Existing terminals keep their current runtime.' With live terminals or active tasks the pane warns '{{value0}} will keep running in the current runtime. Let tasks finish or restart terminals before continuing.', and a change stays pending ('Runtime change pending. New project work will use the selected runtime after you apply.') with 'Cancel' and 'Apply runtime change' buttons.

rows.label: WSL distro
rows.notes: Shown under the Project runtime control only when WSL is selected. Placeholder 'Select distro'. Writes {kind:'wsl', distro}. Disabled while loading or when WSL is unavailable.

rows.label: Keep Fork Up to Date
rows.description: When this fork is behind upstream, Kingu can safely fast-forward its default branch. Kingu skips the update if the branch has local-only commits or conflicts.
rows.notes: Git repos only, and only when repo.upstream is set (a GitHub fork). The searchable description is 'Safely fast-forward this fork from upstream.' The row shows 'Fork of {{owner}}/{{repo}}'. The default is 'ask'. Choosing Safe Auto also runs a sync immediately. Options are disabled while syncing. The segmented aria-label is 'Fork sync mode'.

rows.label: Sync Now
rows.notes: Action inside Keep Fork Up to Date (reads 'Syncing' while running). Fast-forwards the fork's default branch from upstream and toasts the result: 'Fork updated' / 'Fork already up to date' / 'Fork sync skipped' (with a reason) / 'Fork sync failed'.

rows.label: External worktrees
rows.description: Override whether worktrees created outside Kingu appear for this project.
rows.notes: Git repos only. 'global' writes null (clears the override). The helper line shows 'Using global: Show|Hide' when not overridden, or 'Global default: Show|Hide' when overridden. The global default comes from GlobalSettings worktreeVisibilityDefaults.external for the repo's owning host (legacy repos default to show). Refreshes worktrees after the change.

rows.label: Default Worktree Base
rows.description: Default base branch or ref when creating worktrees.
rows.notes: Git repos only. BaseRefPicker shows the effective ref (or 'No default base ref') and a status line: 'Pinned for this repo', 'Following primary branch ({{value0}})' or 'Pick a base branch below'. With multiple remotes it adds a hint: 'Multiple remotes detected. Type a remote name (e.g. upstream) or a full ref (e.g. upstream/main) to scope results.' A search input ('Search branches by name...', 2+ chars, 200ms debounce) lists matching refs; clicking one sets worktreeBaseRef. Search states: 'Searching branches...' and 'No matching branches found.' The 'Use Primary' button (disabled when not pinned) clears worktreeBaseRef to undefined.

rows.label: Worktree Location
rows.description: Project-specific directory for new worktrees.
rows.notes: Git repos only. Saves on blur (trimmed; empty = undefined; skipped when unchanged). The placeholder is GlobalSettings workspaceDir. Helper: 'Relative paths resolve from this project root.' A 'Use Global' ghost button appears when set and clears it to undefined.

sections.title: Worktree Hooks
sections.description: Scripts that run when worktrees are created or archived. Local scripts are stored on this machine; `kingu.yaml` scripts are shared with your team.
sections.notes: Git repos only. The section stays hidden while a search matches none of its entries (Setup Script, Archive Script, Advanced, When to Run Setup, Custom GitHub Issue Command). Hook settings persist as repo.hookSettings via updateRepo. Script drafts autosave after 700ms and on blur, and policy changes persist immediately. The shared scripts come from kingu.yaml in the repo root and are read-only here.

rows.label: Setup Script
rows.description: Runs after a new worktree is created; install deps, copy env files, run migrations.
rows.notes: The searchable description is 'Local and shared scripts that run after a new worktree is created.' Env var chips carry tooltips: $KINGU_ROOT_PATH, $KINGU_WORKTREE_PATH, $KINGU_WORKSPACE_NAME ('Available environment variables (hover for details):'). When kingu.yaml defines scripts.setup, a read-only preview appears, badged 'kingu.yaml - shared with your team' with the hint 'Edit kingu.yaml to change.', and the local editor is hidden behind an 'Add local script' button until the user adds one; the local editor is then badged 'local - just for you, on this machine'. Placeholder: '# e.g. pnpm install cp "$KINGU_ROOT_PATH/.env" "$KINGU_WORKTREE_PATH/.env"'. Footer: 'Runs as a single shell script. Saved on this machine.' A save indicator shows 'Saving...' / 'Saved'.

rows.label: When to run
rows.description: Default behavior when a new worktree is created.
rows.notes: The searchable title is 'When to Run Setup' ('Choose the default behavior when a setup script is available.'). The default is run-by-default. Option tooltips: 'Prompt before running setup.' / 'Run setup automatically.' / 'Only run setup when chosen.'

rows.label: Wait for setup to complete before starting agent
rows.description: Turn this on when setup installs dependencies, MCP servers, or config files the agent needs during startup.
rows.notes: Sits in the same card as 'When to run'. The default is start-immediately (off).

rows.label: Archive Script
rows.description: Runs before a worktree is archived or removed.
rows.notes: The searchable description is 'Local and shared scripts that run before a worktree is archived.' It behaves like Setup Script: shared kingu.yaml scripts.archive preview, 'Add local script', env chips. Placeholder: '# e.g. echo "Cleaning up $KINGU_WORKSPACE_NAME"'.

rows.label: Local scripts will not run
rows.description: Local scripts are saved, but Script Source is set to kingu.yaml only.
rows.notes: Conditional warning, shown only when a local setup or archive script exists and the effective command source is shared-only. Before the kingu.yaml inspection is ready it reads 'Local scripts are saved. Kingu is still checking kingu.yaml before it can recommend which script source to use.' with a 'Checking...' pill. After that it shows one button: 'Run both' (when kingu.yaml has scripts) or 'Use local commands' (when it has none), which sets commandSourcePolicy.

rows.label: Custom GitHub Issue Command
rows.description: Optional override. Use {{artifact_url}} for the linked issue or PR URL.
rows.notes: Stored outside Repo and GlobalSettings: the per-user file {repoRoot}/.kingu/issue-command, read and written via the runtime hooks client on the selected host; main adds .kingu to .gitignore. The searchable description is 'Optional per-user override for the linked-issue command.' Placeholder 'Complete {{artifact_url}}'. Saves on blur (trimmed) and on unmount. Footer: 'Leave blank to use the repo default from kingu.yaml' followed by '.' when kingu.yaml has an issueCommand, else 'when one exists.' Save errors show inline and as a toast.

rows.label: Command Source
rows.description: When both kingu.yaml and local commands exist, choose which run.
rows.notes: Inside the collapsible 'Advanced' details block (searchable title 'Advanced', description 'Command source and kingu.yaml details.'). The summary reads 'Advanced · Command source & kingu.yaml' with a pill naming the current policy. It is forced open when the search matches. The options are three card buttons with descriptions: 'Run only committed repo commands; ignore local commands.' / 'Ignore kingu.yaml; run only your local commands.' / 'kingu.yaml first, then your local commands.' The effective default comes from resolveHookCommandSourcePolicy(stored, {hasLocalScript}).

rows.label: kingu.yaml status
rows.description: Dynamic: 'Using `kingu.yaml`' | '`kingu.yaml` could not be parsed' | 'No `kingu.yaml` detected'
rows.notes: Read-only status card inside Advanced, below Command Source. loaded: 'Shared hook and issue-automation defaults are defined in the repo and available to everyone who uses it.' plus a YAML preview of scripts/issueCommand. update-available: 'The file contains configuration keys that this version of Kingu does not recognize...'. invalid: 'The core configuration file exists in the repo root, but Kingu could not parse the supported hook definitions yet.' plus a numbered list of fixes. missing: 'Add an `kingu.yaml` file to enable shared setup, archive, or issue-automation defaults for this repo. Example template:'. The non-loaded states include an 'Example kingu.yaml template' block with a 'Copy' / 'Copied' button that copies a template to the clipboard (action, nothing is written).

sections.title: Source Control AI
sections.description: These overrides apply to this project setup and inherit the client Source Control AI defaults until customized.
sections.notes: Git repos only (searchable entry 'Git AI Author'). All rows write repo.sourceControlAi (RepoSourceControlAiOverrides) via updateRepo. Selects persist immediately. Each action recipe's CLI args and command template are drafted until that recipe's Save. Inherited values come from GlobalSettings sourceControlAi (and legacy commitMessageAi) and defaultTuiAgent. A save error shows under the header.

rows.label: Show Source Control AI actions
rows.description: Controls whether Source Control AI buttons are shown for this repository. Generation used by separate features follows those features' settings. Global default is {{value0}}.
rows.notes: inherit = undefined, on = true, off = false. value0 is Show or Hide from GlobalSettings sourceControlAi.enabled.

rows.label: Custom command
rows.description: Repo fallback for text actions that select Custom command.
rows.notes: A mode select plus a monospace text input below it. The placeholder is the global customAgentCommand, or 'e.g. ollama run llama3.1 {prompt}'. Switching to Repository command pre-fills from the global command. The input saves on blur, and empty = inherit (cleared).

rows.label: Action recipes: Commit message
rows.description: Generate the commit message from staged changes.
rows.notes: The per-action card sits under the 'Action recipes' label. Status line: 'Using global settings' or 'Customized for this repository'; 'Kingu default prompt' / 'Global custom prompt' / 'Repository custom prompt'; 'Global custom args' / 'Repository custom args' / 'No args'. The mode select enables three sub-controls, all disabled until Customize: an 'Agent' select ('Use default agent', 'Custom command' for text actions only, plus catalog agents), a 'CLI arguments' input (placeholder = inherited args or the agent-specific default, e.g. '--model sonnet'), and a 'Command template' textarea (placeholder = inherited template, default '{basePrompt}') with variable chips. When customized, the footer reads 'Unsaved changes' or 'Saved', with 'Discard' and 'Save' ('Saving...') buttons. Text action, so the Custom command agent is offered.

rows.label: Action recipes: Pull request details
rows.description: Generate the hosted review title and description.
rows.notes: Same card layout as Commit message. Text action (Custom command agent offered).

rows.label: Action recipes: Branch name
rows.description: Rename Kingu-created branches from the initial agent task.
rows.notes: Same card layout. Text action (Custom command agent offered).

rows.label: Action recipes: Commit failure fixes
rows.description: Start an agent when a commit hook or git commit fails.
rows.notes: Same card layout. Launch action (no Custom command agent option).

rows.label: Action recipes: Push failure fixes
rows.description: Start an agent when a pre-push hook or git push fails.
rows.notes: Same card layout. Launch action.

rows.label: Action recipes: Broken checks fixes
rows.description: Start an agent from failed hosted-review checks.
rows.notes: Same card layout. Launch action.

rows.label: Action recipes: Conflict resolution
rows.description: Start an agent for local or hosted-review merge conflicts.
rows.notes: Same card layout. Launch action.

rows.label: Action recipes: Review comment resolution
rows.description: Start an agent from selected unresolved PR or MR comments.
rows.notes: Same card layout. Launch action.

rows.label: Draft by default
rows.description: Global default is On|Off.
rows.notes: Under the 'Hosted-review creation defaults' label. inherit = null/undefined. The global value comes from GlobalSettings sourceControlAi.prCreationDefaults.draft.

rows.label: Use review template when available
rows.description: Global default is On|Off.
rows.notes: Hosted-review creation defaults.

rows.label: Generate details when opening Create PR
rows.description: Global default is On|Off.
rows.notes: Hosted-review creation defaults.

rows.label: Open hosted review after creation
rows.description: Global default is On|Off.
rows.notes: Hosted-review creation defaults.

sections.title: Worktree Shared Paths
sections.description: When a new worktree is created, each path listed here is APFS clone-copied on macOS when possible, otherwise symlinked from the primary checkout.
sections.notes: Git repos only, and hidden for SSH repos (repo.connectionId set). The searchable description is 'Paths to materialize from the primary checkout into newly created worktrees.'

rows.label: Linked paths
rows.notes: The 'Add Path' button opens a combobox popover (placeholder 'Type a path (e.g. .env or node_modules)…'). It suggests top-level entries of the repo root (local host only), marks existing entries 'added', and offers 'Add <typed>' for free text; the empty state reads 'No matches. Keep typing to add a custom path.' Leading slashes are stripped and duplicates ignored. Paths render as removable chips (aria 'Remove {{value0}}') under 'Linked paths' with a count of '1 path' or '{{value0}} paths'. Empty state: 'No shared paths configured for this repository.'

sections.title: Sparse Checkout Presets
sections.description: Manage saved directory sets for sparse worktree creation.
sections.notes: Git repos only. Presets are stored in persisted app state sparsePresetsByRepo[repoId] (via fetchSparsePresets / saveSparsePreset / removeSparsePreset), not in Repo or GlobalSettings.

rows.label: New Preset
rows.description: Saved directories are used when creating sparse worktrees for this repository.
rows.notes: Disabled while a draft is open. It opens an inline editor titled 'New Preset' (or 'Edit Preset'). The editor has a 'Name' input (placeholder 'e.g. web-only', max 80; errors 'Name is required.', 'Name must be 80 characters or fewer.' and '"<name>" already exists.') and a 'Directories' textarea (placeholder 'packages/web shared/ui'). The textarea helper reads '1 directory will be saved.' or '{{value0}} directories will be saved.', then 'Use repo-relative paths like packages/web or apps/api.' Buttons: 'Cancel', 'Save Preset', and an X ('Cancel preset edit').

rows.label: Saved presets
rows.notes: Each preset row shows its name, '1 directory' / '{{value0}} directories', 'Updated {{value0}}' / 'Updated date unknown', and a directory preview. It has an edit (pencil) button and a 'Delete' button that needs a second click ('Confirm', then 'Deleting'). States: 'Loading sparse presets...', 'Sparse presets could not be loaded.', and the empty 'No sparse presets saved for this repository.' Errors appear in a red alert box.

sections.title: MCP Configs
sections.description: Inspect MCP server definitions that agents can use while working in this repo.
sections.notes: Git repos only. Read-only inspection of MCP config files in the active worktree of this repo (or its main worktree). SSH repos add the line 'SSH repos are read through the remote filesystem. Starter creation is limited to the workspace root config.' and need a live connection ('Connect this SSH repo to inspect or add MCP configs.'). Other unavailable states: 'This workspace path is not available from this host.' / 'This workspace path is not available on disk.'

rows.label: Refresh MCP configs
rows.notes: Icon button that re-inspects the config files.

rows.label: Add MCP config
rows.notes: Shown only when no config exists and inspection is available. The first click changes the label to 'Create empty config' (the confirmation resets after 3s); the second writes a starter .mcp.json at the worktree root, opens it in the editor, and toasts 'MCP config created'. This writes a file, not a setting.

rows.label: Detected configs
rows.notes: The header reads '<n> detected · <m> server(s)'. Checked candidates: Workspace (.mcp.json), Cursor (.cursor/mcp.json), Claude (.claude.json), Claude workspace (.claude/mcp.json). Each found or invalid file gets a row with its label, path, a status pill ('Unreadable', 'Not found', 'Invalid JSON', 'No servers' or '<n> server(s)'), an 'Open' button (opens the file in the editor), and the servers with transport, url/command and env. Missing candidates are listed under 'Checked'. Empty state: 'No MCP config found. Add an empty workspace config when you want this repo to define its own MCP servers.'
